items.title: U.S. companies are dropping climate targets, Harvard data reveals
items.summary: The number of U.S. companies with climate targets peaked in 2022 and has fallen since, according to a newly released database compiled by Harvard University researchers.

items.title: How leading buyers got finance to say “yes” on nature-based carbon removals
items.summary: Carbon markets have transformed over the past five years, with updated standards and rigorous due diligence frameworks giving sustainability leaders much more confidence in project design.

items.title: £4bn added to UK electricity costs as gas power profits surged during energy crisis, research finds
items.summary: New research has found that gas-fired power stations made £4.1bn in additional profits during the 2021 and 2022 energy crisis, while higher gas prices pushed up electricity bills for consumers.

items.title: Action Agenda: COP31 Presidency sets 35-by-35 global electrification pledge and AI climate action initiative
items.summary: The COP31 Presidency has formally unveiled a pledge to increase the share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035, as well as launching an initiative to ensure AI is harnessed in a way that can assist with climate action.

items.title: Companies brace for $400bn future water risk costs
items.summary: Companies are signalling nearly half a trillion dollars in future financial pain from water disruption. Yet, analysis of thousands of corporate disclosures reveals a striking gap in preparedness.

items.title: Corporates warn of renewables shortfall in meeting clean energy goals
items.summary: Global businesses have warned that market and procurement barriers are hindering progress towards 100% renewables commitments and are failing to shield organisations from volatile energy prices.

items.title: Analysis: ‘Super El Niño’ reaches ‘remarkable’ all-time record
items.summary: This year’s so-called “super El Niño” is entering into record-breaking territory.
